title: Schematic symbols (Figure G7-1)
idea: Figure G7-1 is one circuit with 11 numbered symbols. The exam asks about five of them; the wrong answers point at the look-alikes.

rows: Circle with a bar and an arrow on the gate lead
Circle, arrow on the emitter pointing out
Two coils with straight lines between them
One coil with a wire from its middle

parts.name: Field effect transistor (FET)
parts.look: A circle with a straight bar inside and an arrow pointing in on the gate lead.

parts.name: NPN junction transistor
parts.look: A circle with the base bar and an arrow on the emitter pointing out. Not Pointing iN = NPN.

parts.name: Varactor (variable capacitance) diode
parts.look: A diode with a capacitor's curved plate beside the bar. A look-alike for the Zener.

parts.name: Zener diode
parts.look: A diode whose bar is bent at both ends, like a Z.

parts.name: Solid core transformer
parts.look: Two coils side by side with straight lines (the solid core) between them.

parts.name: Tapped inductor
parts.look: A single coil with a wire coming off partway along it: the tap.

parts.name: Potentiometer
parts.look: A resistor zigzag with an arrow touching its side. Not an inductor.

traps.why: Symbol 2 has an arrow on an emitter: a junction (bipolar) transistor.
Symbol 4 has a capacitor plate: a varactor. The Zener's bar is bent.
Symbol 7 is one coil with a tap. A transformer has two coils.
Symbol 6 has two windings and a core: the transformer.
